setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97 on steps 1 to 4. Channel 2 does not play yet; in the next step you set it up on MIDI port 2, channel 2 with the same pattern. A saved MIDI map is loaded with two relative controls that both accumulate: CC 20 edits the velocity mask of the selected channel and CC 21 edits the velocity mask of channel 2. Both velocity masks are Off (X) and the norns shows channel 1's Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Set up channel 2: select it (2,1), open its Device page and set its output to port 2, MIDI channel 2 with E2 and E3, press K3, give it pattern 1 with (1,2) and hold step 1 then tap step 4 to loop four steps. Select channel 1 (1,1), tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 (port 1) and channel 2 (port 2) both play velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97: no control has been moved yet.
steps.title: Hear both channels before any CC

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks for channel 1 and select the Velocity cell, which reads X. Channel 1 is selected. Send CC 20 with value 65 eleven times (the strip shows eleven control changes). For a relative (binary offset) control, 65 means one step up, 63 means one step down and 0 also counts as down. The velocity mask starts at X, so the first step reaches 0 and the eleventh reaches 10: the Velocity cell now reads 10.
steps.title: CC 20 on the selected channel 1

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 1 now plays every note at velocity 10. Channel 2 is unchanged.
steps.title: Hear channel 1 at velocity 10

steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 twice and tap Play: channel 1 comes down from 10 to 8 and plays every note at velocity 8. Channel 2 is still unchanged.
steps.title: CC 20 down twice

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Masks screen stays open and its Velocity cell reads X for channel 2. Send CC 20 with value 65 three times: the cell reads 2. A selected-channel control follows the channel you select.
steps.title: Select channel 2, CC 20 follows

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 2 now plays at velocity 2 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 2

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) to select it. Its Velocity cell still reads 8. Send CC 21 with value 65 twice, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look: its Velocity cell reads 4, up from 2. CC 21 is mapped to channel 2 itself, so it ignores which channel is selected.
steps.title: CC 21 ignores the selection

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 4 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 4

steps.caption: Send CC 21 with value 0, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look. Any value below 64 is a decrease, so its Velocity cell drops from 4 to 3.
steps.title: CC 21 value 0 steps down

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) again and tap Play. Channel 2 plays at velocity 3 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 3

title: A loaded map follows the selected or fixed channel
